newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK JULY RPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK JULY RPI.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' comments about UK retail prices. Headline inflation rose 3.3 percent year-on-year, RPIX 3.0 percent year on year and RPIY 2.2 percent.
"One factor that may prevent the market selling off too badly on this is that RPIY fell on the month.
That measure strips out the tax effects from the budget and suggests much if the damamge is ebing done by mortgage rates and tax effects."

"The headline figures are generally worse than expected. Some offsets, however, in that clothing and footwear inflation is very low, as is household goods inflation and those are components of retail sales where demand has been strongest of late. The market may take some relief in the services inflation has fallen back from 3.2 to 2.9 percent. Although the headline numbers have been distorted by duty effects and by seasonal food prices, there is no evidence in these figures of any demand led inflationary pressure."

"I think we are at the peak in terms of interest rates and that the rate rises we have had already, along with the fiscal tightening from the budget, will be enough to get inflation under control and on target next year."

"The data look very bad. I think we're getting higher readings due to the increases in excise duties which are feeding through more than the market had expected. Even so it is a disappointing report and the fall in the prices of clothing and footwear are not as impressive as they might seem."
